clue.text: Drive by Liberal party to enlist Independent?

indicators.note: to enlist is to take someone into the ranks, so one letter is drawn inside the others

parts.note: a DO is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Liberal campaign drive persuading an Independent candidate to join the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual drive or urge, a psychological impulse.

clue.text: Such generosity found in Sweden or Switzerland, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the description is said aloud

parts.note: both country names begin with a large, capital letter ess

explanation.surface: A remark that Swedes or the Swiss are notably generous.
explanation.walkthrough: The common feature of the two names is a capital S at the start: said out loud, 'large ess'.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, munificence.

clue.text: Nomad finding place to sleep? That's right — in Paris, to the north

parts.note: a bed is a place to sleep
oui is French for yes, that's right

explanation.surface: A nomad looking for somewhere to sleep, told yes in Paris to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bedouin is a nomadic desert Arab.

clue.text: See frogmen coming to the surface in various ways

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming to the surface puts the frogmen above, on top of, the See

parts.note: frogmen are underwater divers
Ely is a cathedral city whose bishop's see is often used in crosswords

explanation.surface: Watch the frogmen surfacing in different spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a verb but a bishop's see: Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversely means variously, in different manners.

clue.text: He's penned The Woman In White overture

indicators.note: penned means enclosed as in a pen, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
a bride is traditionally the woman dressed in white at a wedding

explanation.surface: A claim that some man wrote The Woman in White, the Wilkie Collins novel, plus an overture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Woman In White' looks like the Collins novel title, but it simply means a bride; 'penned' looks like 'wrote' but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's concert overture is named after the Scottish islands, also called Fingal's Cave.

clue.text: Tabloid's power revealed in book

parts.note: an empire is a dominion or sphere of power
The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, so of The Sun means belonging to the tabloid

explanation.surface: A tabloid's influence is exposed in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; 'power of the Sun' is the title of J. G. Ballard's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballard's novel of a boy interned by the Japanese in Shanghai, filmed by Spielberg.

clue.text: Who might be responsible for some more belligerence?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about who is to blame for some growing aggression.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is the sort of figure blamed for unrest and fighting.

clue.text: Computer replaced by dept's OK

indicators.note: replaced suggests putting the letters back in a different order

explanation.surface: A department approves replacing its computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is a personal computer for use on a desk.

clue.text: Youngster recruited by top regiment given healthy food

indicators.note: recruited by means taken in by, so the youngster goes inside the regiment

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's elite Special Air Service regiment
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A young recruit to an elite regiment is fed healthily.
explanation.definitionFit: Salads are dishes of raw vegetables, considered wholesome eating.

clue.text: Adopts aloof attitude, creating incomprehensible dramas?

definitions.meaning: pretends to be uninterested, especially in a suitor
stage works that are difficult to understand

explanation.surface: Someone acts standoffish by writing baffling theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning indifference is the idiom's sense; read literally, the phrase describes plays difficult for audiences to grasp.

clue.text: Wanting reform, peer loved change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A lord who wants political reform and is fond of change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' is a link word here: the clue wants the reform the anagram gives.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform an area or building is to rebuild or remodel it, synonym for this.

clue.text: Headquarters next to lake in Swiss city

parts.note: a base is a headquarters or centre of operations
L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A firm's headquarters beside a lake in a Swiss city.
explanation.definitionFit: Basel is a city on the Rhine in northern Switzerland.

clue.text: Duke ultimately has question about queen's household officer

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Duke
about here means surrounding, so the word for question goes round the queen

parts.note: a query is a question
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A duke finally has a query about one of the queen's household staff.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer attending a member of the British royal family.

clue.text: Told about daughter and others doing a turn

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived for about or concerning

indicators.note: doing a turn means turning round, so the daughter and others are read backwards

parts.note: et al. is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: Gossip about a daughter and her friends performing a stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a turn' reverses D plus ETAL to make LATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have related a story is to have told or narrated it.

clue.text: Dowsing evidently limits fire damage

indicators.note: the words Dowsing evidently enclose, or limit, the run of letters wanted

explanation.surface: Dousing a fire evidently limits the damage it does.
explanation.walkthrough: Dowsing (water divining) is spelt to suggest dousing a fire; the run sits across 'Dowsing evidently'.
explanation.definitionFit: A singe is a slight burn, the mild damage a flame causes.

clue.text: Words of advice on how to catch flighty creatures

parts.note: to hook a fish is to catch it
tips are helpful words of advice

explanation.surface: Advice on how to catch flighty creatures, like an angler's or a butterfly hunter's guide.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as advice on how to hook something; the answer is a family of moths.
explanation.definitionFit: Hook-tips are moths with hooked wing tips, insects that fly about.

clue.text: Vehicle taken over flat surface is easy to control

indicators.note: taken over means turned over, so the vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
a table is a flat surface

explanation.surface: A vehicle driven across a level surface is easy to steer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractable means docile, manageable.

clue.text: Rescued by crew, you start to see sense

indicators.note: rescued by suggests being taken in by, so the pieces go inside the crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew
ye is an old word for you

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of see

explanation.surface: Picked up by a boat's crew, you begin to see again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rescued by' signals containment: the crew is a rowing eight, which takes in the old 'you' plus the opening of 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Scripture worthily rendered in translation

indicators.note: rendering a text in translation reworks it, so the letters of worthily are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scripture rendered worthily when translated into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ is the Bible or other sacred writings.

clue.text: Certainly not patent medicine old boy's obtained at first

indicators.note: obtained at first puts the old boy before the medicine

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
a cure is a medicine or remedy

explanation.surface: A remedy that is certainly not a patent medicine, from an old boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent medicine' suggests a proprietary drug; here patent means obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means plain or evident; obscure is its opposite, hidden or unclear.

clue.text: Dunce always comes last in test

indicators.note: comes last puts the word for always after the dunce

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person, a dunce
AY, or aye, is an old word meaning always

explanation.surface: The class dunce always comes bottom in the test.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay is to test, especially to analyse a metal's purity.

clue.text: Making nasty comments when shooting

definitions.meaning: criticising in a petty, spiteful way

explanation.surface: Making snide remarks while out with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are firing from cover: one with spiteful words, the other with a rifle.

clue.text: British villain's ' accent

parts.note: a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A British villain with a strong accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially Irish or Scottish.

clue.text: Resume painting after break

indicators.note: after puts painting at the end, following the break

parts.note: a rest is a break from work
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: An artist goes back to painting after a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to begin again, to resume.

clue.text: Inspect car's transmission when starting

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

indicators.note: when starting picks the opening letter of transmission

explanation.surface: Checking a car's gearbox when starting it.
explanation.definitionFit: To audit is to examine accounts or a process officially.

clue.text: Examination candidates given directions prior to tests

indicators.note: prior to puts the directions in front of the tests

parts.note: E and N are the compass directions east and north
tries are attempts or tests

explanation.surface: Exam candidates are given instructions before sitting their tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Entries are the people entered for an exam or competition.

clue.text: Fruit to go with tongue, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means almost all, so the language loses its last letter

parts.note: Urdu is a tongue, a language of Pakistan and India

explanation.surface: A fruit that is meant to go well with tongue as a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourd is the hard-skinned fruit of a climbing plant, like a squash.

clue.text: Complaining girl's first put on weird jewellery

indicators.note: first picks only the opening letter of girl

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or weird
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A girl first puts on some odd, showy jewellery and complains.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling is moaning, voicing discontent.

clue.text: Animal, one feeding mostly round hollow

indicators.note: round says the shortened eater surrounds the hollow
mostly drops the final letter of the word for one feeding

parts.note: an eater is one feeding
a dent is a hollow in a surface

explanation.surface: An animal feeding, mostly around a hollow in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one feeding' looks like part of the animal's description, but it is the eater, shortened by 'mostly' and wrapped 'round' the hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: An edentate is a mammal without front teeth, such as a sloth or anteater.

clue.text: Pressure to hang on, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, so it sounds the same as the answer

parts.note: to wait is to hang on

explanation.surface: Being pressed to hang on, say, on a telephone line.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight is pressure or force bearing down on something.
